> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4013e30817f6c7b1eb65226b18c46e4717633440` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5e049350cbaab8f80429710c1f1eb2a0b0c6e985` — the merge of head `d7a38bb7506645ee24f9ce4a490a76e5723d8be2` into base `4013e30817f6c7b1eb65226b18c46e4717633440`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5e049350cbaab8f80429710c1f1eb2a0b0c6e985 && git checkout 5e049350cbaab8f80429710c1f1eb2a0b0c6e985
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4013e30817f6c7b1eb65226b18c46e4717633440 d7a38bb7506645ee24f9ce4a490a76e5723d8be2 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4013e30817f6c7b1eb65226b18c46e4717633440 && git merge --no-ff d7a38bb7506645ee24f9ce4a490a76e5723d8be2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4013e30817f6c7b1eb65226b18c46e4717633440
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4013e30817f6c7b1eb65226b18c46e4717633440` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**Epic red-line review: E1 #31672, head e94f303d · 2026-11-09T01:06Z**

Verdict: **PASS once one small change is in.** It needs no re-review; send the head.

| Red line | Reading |
|---|---|
| 1. Never loosens | `execute()` asks `resolvePackageScopedName` with the calling flow's package (`packagedFlowOwner(context.flowName)`). The environment-only holder (D3 (a)) and the outside-closure holder (D3 step 3) are refused, naming every candidate. There is no fallback and no second resolver. Door, trigger and no-context callers resolve environment-wide, with one-holder names unchanged and pinned. While phase 1 refuses two flow holders, the engine's one flow per name is the resolver's only holder, so a resolved answer and the executed flow agree. |
| 2. Ambiguity reported, never guessed | Outside-closure: refused with candidates. The `ambiguous-*` arm is held back, because it is reachable only through the pre-phase-1 sealed clash, which waits on the maintainer's Q1 `Ruled:` on #31677 (6728850663). The ready patch in the PR body is the right carrier. |
| 3. Independently releasable | (a) green: 3470 package tests and the dogfood VERDICT. (b) pinned. (c) no migration. (d) `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, covering D3 (a) and step 3, 0 first-party, sibling-in-artifact 0. objectql moves to dependencies with no cycle. |

**The change: a held-back refusal is still reported.**
- Today `flowNameRefusal` drops an `ambiguous-*` refusal without a word, and the precedence pick runs.
- Holding back the *act* is right until Q1. Holding back the *report* is not.
- Required: when the resolver refuses with an `ambiguous-*` reason that this child does not act on, warn once per (name, caller), naming every candidate and saying that today's precedence pick still runs until #31677 Q1.
- Add a test that is red without it.

**Recorded obligations:**
- A missing resolver slice (no `objectql` registry) refuses nothing. That is accepted while phase 1 refuses for `flow`. B #31696, which narrows phase 1 for flows, must fail closed on a missing slice or prove every composition carries it. This is the same obligation as E5's (6729233545).
- *Open question, arming both same-named flows:* not S3. It becomes reachable only when phase 1 stops refusing two flow holders, so it is a prerequisite of B #31696: the engine holds and dispatches flows by (package, name) before that backstop narrows. I am noting it on #31696.

The D4 activation projection keyed by (package, name) is accepted: an environment-wide row (`''`) disarms every holder, and a package row disarms only its holder.

Seat 3 accepts and lands this after the change and green CI. It is not a governed surface.
